title: New Hire Velocity and Manager Commitment Agreement
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview:
This document defines the New Hire Velocity metric, the Manager Commitment Agreement (MCA) template used during onboarding and probation, and the operational steps for hiring managers and people-ops to convert new hires into fully operational contributors. The intent is to create a measurable, manager-owned process that increases first-quarter impact while reducing time-to-autonomy and bias in conversion decisions.

Intended audience:
- Hiring managers
- People-ops partners
- People managers onboarding new contributors
- Talent acquisition when closing offers

High-level principles:
- Manager ownership: hiring manager signs an MCA within 72 hours of a new hire’s start date.
- Measurable outcomes: define 3–5 concrete signals of success for the role (velocity metrics + qualitative signals).
- Structured checkpoints: use fixed-day milestones (Day 14, Day 30, Day 60, Day 90) for calibration and interventions.
- Transparency: document assessments and outcomes in the candidate’s onboarding page.
- Remediation before escalation: provide targeted coaching and time-bound interventions before formal probation escalations.

Definitions:
- New Hire Velocity (NHV): a composite, role-adjusted score representing the speed at which a hire achieves core outputs. NHV = weighted sum of Role Ramp % (0–100), Task Turnaround (median days), and Cross-team Signals. People-ops maintains role baseline weights.
- Manager Commitment Agreement (MCA): a short, signed agreement between hiring manager and people-ops outlining expectations, support, and measurable success criteria for the new hire.

Manager Commitment Agreement (MCA) template (fill-in):
1) New hire: [Full name] | Start date: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Role: [IC/Manager/Staff Eng/Product]
2) Onboarding owner(s): [Manager], [Buddy], [People-ops partner]
3) Primary success signals (choose 3–5):
   - Signal A: [e.g., deliver first small scoped PR to production]
   - Signal B: [e.g., complete training curriculum A + pass quiz >= 80%]
   - Signal C: [e.g., lead 1 cross-team sync with clear outcome]
4) Target velocity milestones:
   - Day 14: baseline access + complete orientation + 1st small task assigned
   - Day 30: complete onboarding checklist items 80%+, first PR merged or equivalent
   - Day 60: independent execution on at least one medium-sized deliverable
   - Day 90: sustainable throughput aligning with role-baseline >= 70%
5) Manager commitments (explicit):
   - Weekly 1:1 agenda entries for the first 90 days and written feedback in 24–48 hours after major milestone reviews.
   - Provide buddy support and 4 hours/week protected time for ramp-related learning for first 30 days.
   - Block at least four calibration meetings with cross-functional partners across the first 60 days.
6) People-ops commitments:
   - Coordinate kick-off, ensure access provisioning within 48 hours, and schedule 30/60/90 check-ins.
   - Offer coaching session or calibration facilitator within 7 business days of a low NHV signal.
7) Signatures (place in onboarding doc):
   - Hiring manager: [name, date]
   - People-ops partner: [name, date]

Checkpoints and procedures (operational steps):
1) Pre-start (Talent Acquisition):
   - Share role baseline and NHV expectations with candidate and hiring manager before offer acceptance.
   - Include link to the MCA template in offer packet.
2) Day 0–3 (Kickoff):
   - Manager creates MCA in the hiring page and completes initial fields.
   - People-ops verifies access request, buddy assignment, and schedule for 30/60/90 check-ins.
3) Day 14 (Early signal check):
   - Manager completes short NHV status update (Green/Amber/Red) with brief rationale in the onboarding doc.
   - If Amber/Red: initiate a targeted action plan with specific deadlines (max 14 days) and schedule weekly coaching.
4) Day 30 (First formal review):
   - Run a structured rubric (see Rubric table below).
   - Outcome options: On-track, Needs Support, Reassessment Plan.
5) Day 60 (Progress and calibration):
   - Cross-functional stakeholder feedback is collected and summarized by the manager.
   - If performance is below expectations, initiate People-ops facilitated coaching + 30-day reassessment.
6) Day 90 (Conversion decision):
   - Manager presents evidence vs. MCA signals in a Conversion Brief to People-ops.
   - People-ops records final outcome: Converted / Extended Probation / Offboarding.

Structured assessment rubric (use at Day 30 & Day 90):
- Table: role, criteria, score (1–5), evidence required
| Criteria | Target (examples) | Score 1–5 | Evidence |
| Role knowledge | Understands core product and infra | 4 | Notes from knowledge check, PRs, demo |
| Task delivery | Completes assigned work on time | 3 | PRs, ticket resolution timestamps |
| Collaboration | Clear cross-team communication | 4 | Meeting summaries, stakeholder emails |
| Learning velocity | Completes training & applies learnings | 4 | Training completion, applied fixes |
| Ownership & initiative | Proactively identifies and resolves issues | 3 | Incidents handled, suggestions made |

Scoring guidance: 4–5 = On-track; 3 = Borderline (needs coaching); 1–2 = At-risk (requires action plan).

Decision matrix (Day 90):
- Average score >= 3.8 and NHV >= 70% -> Convert
- Average score 3.0–3.79 or NHV 50–69% -> Extend probation 30 days with focused plan
- Average score < 3.0 or NHV < 50% -> Convene offboarding/role-change discussion

Manager playbook: concrete steps for a manager at each milestone:
- Before start: draft MCA and role-specific success signals with input from team leads.
- Week 1: run orientation, ensure first small deliverable is scope-locked, set weekly 1:1 cadence.
- Week 2–4: provide daily briefings for the first two weeks, transition to weekly written checkpoints after Day 14.
- Month 1 Review: use rubric, record evidence links, decide on green/amber/red and next steps.
- Month 2: focus on cross-team deliverables and evidence of autonomy.
- Month 3: complete conversion brief and present for people-ops review.

Template: Conversion brief (one-page):
- Candidate name, role, start date
- MCA success signals and progress summary
- NHV at Day 30/60/90 (numbers & short interpretation)
- Evidence links: PRs, tickets, peer feedback
- Manager recommendation and rationale

Remediation & coaching playbook (when NHV is amber/red):
1) Triage call within 48 hours with People-ops + Manager + Buddy (30 minutes).
2) Draft a 14-day focused improvement plan: explicit tasks, learning resources, success criteria.
3) Schedule twice-weekly short checkpoints; document outcomes.
4) If insufficient progress at end of 14 days, escalate to a 30-day formal reassessment with a People-ops facilitator.

Operational templates (examples you can copy):
- CLI snippet to create onboarding page via infra tool (example):
  rwi onboarding create --name \"[Name]\" --role \"[Role]\" --start \"YYYY-MM-DD\" --manager \"[Manager email]\"

- Small JSON example for MCA fields used by the people-ops system: 
  {"candidate_name": "[Name]", "start_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "manager": "[email]", "signals": ["deliver_pr", "training_pass"]}

Equity and bias safeguards:
- Require at least two documented evidence items for any negative conversion decision.
- Use anonymized calibration panels for borderline cases where possible.
- People-ops will ensure consistent role baselines are used across teams to reduce manager-by-manager variance.

Hiring manager responsibilities (summary table):
| Phase | Responsibilities | SLA |
| Pre-start | Draft MCA, confirm buddy | Before Day 0 |
| Kickoff | Populate onboarding page, assign tasks | Day 0–3 (48–72h) |
| Early Check | Submit Day 14 status | Day 14 |
| Formal Reviews | Day 30/60/90 rubric reviews and evidence | Day 30/60/90 |

Escalation & exceptions:
- If manager unavailability prevents scheduled reviews, assign backup reviewer (senior IC or upward manager) within 5 business days.
- For international hires with local compliance requirements, people-ops will attach country-specific timeframes to the MCA.

Analytics & dashboards:
- People-ops will maintain a live dashboard with NHV distribution, time-to-first-PR, and converted % by cohort.
- Monthly calibration reviews will surface managers with outlier conversion rates for coaching.

Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: What if a role is primarily non-code (design/research/customer success)?
A: Replace PR-based signals with role-appropriate deliverables (research brief, customer playbook, closed CS ticket). The MCA must use comparable complexity/impact signals.

Q: Who owns final conversion?
A: The hiring manager recommends; people-ops records and validates process adherence. For escalations, the people-ops partner runs calibration and signs off.

Appendix: example 14-day focused improvement plan (copyable):
- Objective: Complete onboarding training module X and ship change Y to staging
- Tasks: Module X completion, pair session with buddy (2x 1-hour), submit PR for change Y, stakeholder demo
- Success criteria: Module quiz >= 80%, PR merged to staging, demo recorded
- Checkpoints: Day 7 checkpoint (manager), Day 14 outcome (manager + people-ops)
